title: Allow streamlit app to be run as a normal python script with `python app.py`
body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar feature requests.
- [X] I added a descriptive title and summary to this issue.

### Summary

It would be convenient to allow users to simply run `python streamlit_app.py`, without having to necessarily run `streamlit run streamlit_app.py`



### Why?

This would make it easier to launch streamlit apps in a more flexible way. My particular interest is being able to do `uv run streamlit_app.py` and use [inline script dependencies](https://peps.python.org/pep-0723/) to share completely standalone single-file streamlit apps that don't require any setup other than installing uv.

This can be accomplished today by adding some code that grabs the streamlit internal method that gets run with `streamlit run` and calling that directly, but it would be much nicer if this was the default behavior:

The dependencies above were inserted to the script automatically with:
```sh
uv add --script app.py yfinance
uv add --script app.py streamlit
```

```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.10"
# dependencies = [
#     "streamlit",
#     "yfinance",
# ]
# ///

import streamlit as st
import yfinance as yf

msft = yf.Ticker("MSFT")

# get all stock info
st.write(msft.info)

# Hacky stuff required to be added to make it work without `streamlit run`:
if __name__ == "__main__":
    from streamlit.runtime.scriptrunner import get_script_run_ctx
    if get_script_run_ctx() is None:
        from streamlit.web.cli import main
        import sys
        sys.argv = ['streamlit', 'run', __file__]
        main()
```

As-is, this works simply by:
1. Installing uv
2. Running `uv run app.py`

No other setup is needed at all.

### How?

`python streamlit_app.py` or `python -m streamlit_app` just work, automatically calling the `main` function if streamlit is imported in them.

### Additional Context

_No response_

yes, it works. thanks!

A caveat related to using 3rd party components: ensure you import any 3rd party components **after** doing `streamlit.web.bootstrap.run`. This is because when a component is declared, which typically happens when they're imported, it requires a `ScriptRunContext` (at least on 1.45.0), which is populated by the bootstrap code. A failure to do so will result in the component being replaced by a warning along the lines of:

>Your app is having trouble loading the **st_custom_component.some_comp** component.
>
>If this is an installed component that works locally, the app may be having trouble accessing the component frontend assets due to network latency or proxy settings in your app deployment.
>
>For more troubleshooting help, please see the [Streamlit Component docs](https://docs.streamlit.io/develop/concepts/custom-components) or visit our [forums](https://discuss.streamlit.io/).

To summarize:

```python
from st_custom_component import some_comp  # <<<<<<< BAD

def main():
    some_comp()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "__streamlitmagic__" not in locals():
        from streamlit.web.bootstrap import run

        run(__file__, False, [], {})

    main()
```
```python
def main():
    from st_custom_component import some_comp  # <<<<<<< GOOD

    some_comp()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    if "__streamlitmagic__" not in locals():
        from streamlit.web.bootstrap import run

        run(__file__, False, [], {})

    main()
```

It runs properly with uv, but I see this warning message

```
Thread 'MainThread': missing ScriptRunContext! This warning can be ignored when running in bare mode.
```

This is how I end up with.

Instead of merging main python script file and streamlit entrypoint file, I separated those into two dedicated files.

```python
# app/main.py
from streamlit.web import bootstrap

from app import entrypoint

def streamlit_run(flag_options):
    """simplified version of `streamlit.web.cli._main_run()`"""

    bootstrap.load_config_options(flag_options=flag_options)
    bootstrap.run(entrypoint.__file__, False, [], flag_options)
    # you can of course just hard-code the streamlit entrypoint file path instead:
    # bootstrap.run("app/entrypoint.py", False, [], flag_options)

def main():

    # setup global states like shared loggers here

    streamlit_run({
        # NOTE: hard-coded streamlit options
        #       we can't use streamlit environment variables because we are bypassing
        #       `streamlit run` command and directly calling `bootstrap.run()` to set global loggers.
        "browser.serverAddress": "localhost",
        "server.address": "0.0.0.0",
        "server.headless": True,
    })

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

```python
# entrypoint.py

# streamlit entrypoint file.
# can be executed with `streamlit run entrypoint.py`
# though you might loose some global states then

def main():
    import streamlit as st # put this under `main()` so that it won't be executed on `import app.entrypoint`

    pg = st.navigation([
        st.Page("../pages/1_first_page.py"),
        st.Page("../pages/2_second_page.py"),
    ])
    pg.run()

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

Still compatible with `uv`.

If anyone's trying to register project entry point to use with `uv`, i.e. 
```toml
[project.scripts]
my_dashboard = "my_package.my_dashboard.main:main"
```
you'll need to put the workaround in a function and replace `locals` with `globals`:
```python
def main() -> None:
    if "__streamlitmagic__" not in globals():   # <<<<< changed here
        from streamlit.web.bootstrap import run

        run(__file__, False, [], {})

    # Rest of your init code
```
Then it's possible to do `uv run my_dashboard`. HOWEVER, I am yet to find a way to get it to automatically switch to the `my_package/my_dashboard` subfolder (I don't want to specify this in the run command), so if you have a `.streamlit` folder with configs/secrets, it **won't be picked up** unless you `cd` to the app's directory manually beforehand.

I'll reach out to Astral and update.

## Update

This use case is addressed by the new `st.App(...).run()` API shipping in Streamlit 1.59.

This gives Streamlit apps an officially supported Python entry point, so launcher files can be run directly with:

```bash
python app.py
uv run app.py
```

It also works well with PEP 723 inline script dependencies, e.g. a launcher can declare `streamlit` and app-specific dependencies directly in the file and be run with `uv run app.py` without a separate environment setup step.

Example:

```python
# /// script
# dependencies = [
#   "streamlit",
#   "yfinance",
# ]
# ///

import streamlit as st

app = st.App("streamlit_app.py")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    app.run()
```

This avoids relying on internal `streamlit.web.bootstrap` calls. The supported pattern is a small Python launcher that points at the Streamlit app script, rather than making arbitrary Streamlit scripts auto-run themselves.
